subject: Re: Throughput & latency targets - follow-up and sizing details
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finexcap.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput / latency follow-up from today

Hi Alex / team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can produce a sizing estimate: 

Recap:
- Primary workload: user-facing risk summaries and short Q&A over transactions.
- Expected steady-state: ~50 QPS of inference calls (user requests) across US region.
- Peak: short spikes up to ~220 QPS for 5-10 minutes, roughly 2-3 times/hour during batch ingestion windows.
- Typical prompt size: 30 tokens average. Expected generated response: ~150 tokens on average (some up to ~600 tokens for deep summaries).
- Streaming: yes — you mentioned wanting partial results for the larger summaries so the UX shows progressive answers.
- Latency SLO: business asks ~95th percentile end-to-end < 1.5s for the 150-token responses.

What we need to finalize sizing:
1) Confirmation on concurrency model: are requests single-shot per user (one call per user action), or do you fan-out multiple model calls per request? If fan-out, how many parallel calls on average?
2) Expected tokens/sec per request during generation: we can compute as (tokens_generated / response_time). If you have any traces or approximate response times observed today, please share.
3) Clarify peak traffic distribution: is 220 QPS a sustained peak for 5-10 minutes total across all endpoints or per specific endpoint?
4) Any hard constraints on cold-starts, warm pools, or pre-warmed capacity during scheduled events?

Next steps from our side: if you confirm the items above, I'll run a quick throughput estimate (tokens/sec and required GPU count for Dedicated or recommended hosted sizing) and attach the spreadsheet. I can also model two scenarios: "steady-state optimized" (cost-focused) and "peak-safe" (SLO-focused with standby capacity).

Attached: redwood-throughput-estimate.xlsx (initial template) — I'll fill numbers once you confirm.

Thanks,
Rafael
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
(415) 555-0134

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finexcap.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@finexcap.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput / latency follow-up from today

Thanks Rafael — good summary. Answers inline below.

1) Concurrency model: mostly single-shot per user. We do have a small fan-out for collage generation where we call the model 3x in parallel (different prompt templates) about 8% of requests. So average parallel calls per user request ~1.08.

2) Tokens/sec / response time: we don't have precise traces yet from our prototype. Based on local tests (CPUs) we see 150-token responses take ~1.8s end-to-end. Goal is to get that down to <1.5s at 95th in production. For sizing, assume generation throughput target of ~120 tokens/sec per request (i.e., typical response generated at ~120 t/s).

3) Peak distribution: 220 QPS is aggregate across all endpoints (not per endpoint). Peaks typically correlated with market open / closing windows and overnight batch loads. Spikes are bursty but usually last ~5-12 minutes, occasionally up to 20 minutes during major reports.

4) Warm pools: we'd like minimal cold-starts — willing to keep reserved capacity during trading hours (8am-6pm PT). For weekends and nights, we can scale down.

Extras: security/compliance team will ask about audit logs and data retention — Priya is the point for that.

Hope this helps — let me know if you want me to dump a sample event stream (anonymized) for you to model.

Best,
Alex Chen
Product Lead, Finex Capital
alex.chen@finexcap.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finexcap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput / latency follow-up from today

Alex — perfect, this is exactly what I needed. A couple clarifying points before I finalize the spreadsheet: 

- When you say 120 tokens/sec per request, is that an observed/generator-side throughput (i.e., how fast your current model emits tokens), or a target we'd need to meet in production? We typically size based on tokens/sec and sequence length to estimate per-request GPU-time.
- For the 8% fan-out (3x calls), do those calls occur concurrently within the same user interaction window or are they staggered? Concurrent will increase peak GPU concurrency.
- For the long responses up to 600 tokens, do you require full streaming (token-by-token) or chunked streaming (every 50 tokens)? Chunked streaming can reduce latency sensitivity.

I will produce two rows in the attached workbook: (A) Steady-state: 50 QPS, 30t prompt + 150t response, 120t/s generation; (B) Peak-safe: model concurrency factoring 220 QPS bursts and 8% 3x fan-out. I'll estimate required GPU equivalents for both Hosted and Dedicated.

Proposing a short sync tomorrow (30 min) to walk through the workbook and validate assumptions — Marissa / Michael, can you join? Suggested times: Wed 17 Jun 10:00am PT or 2:30pm PT.

I'll upload the filled workbook to the Drive link and drop a HubSpot note against DEAL-3421.

Thanks,
Rafael
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finexcap.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@finexcap.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput / latency follow-up from today

Alex — thanks for the quick responses. I'm happy to join tomorrow. 10:00am PT works for us; sending a calendar invite in a sec.

Quick next steps / asks from Finex for the pilot scope:
- Pilot window: 2 weeks (production-like traffic replay)
- Success metrics: 95th latency <1.5s for 150-token responses, no more than 2 dropped streaming sessions/hour, and predictable cost per 1k requests within agreed threshold.
- Security: Priya, please let us know any SOC2 / encryption / audit log requirements we should include in the scope.

Rafael — please add the filled workbook to the Drive link and include a brief slide on assumptions (tokens/sec, concurrency factors, peak smoothing strategies). I'll follow up in HubSpot with the proposed pilot SOW and timeline.

Thanks — see you tomorrow,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
